# Agent Conventions

## Generated files

- `src/operations/jira.ts`, `src/operations/confluence.ts`, `src/operations/bitbucket.ts` are generated by `scripts/generate-operations.mjs`. Never hand-edit them.
- `src/operations/registry.json` is generated by the same generator. Never hand-edit it; use `node scripts/generate-operations.mjs`.
- `src/exposure-policy.json` is generated by `rule/build-policy.mjs`. Never hand-edit it; update `rule/source.md` and run the policy builder.
- To change an operation manifest, edit the `OVERRIDES` array in `scripts/generate-operations.mjs` and regenerate.
- `rule/spec-cache/` and its manifest are committed canonical official snapshots. Refresh only with explicit `node rule/fetch-api-inventory.mjs --refresh --bootstrap` or reviewed `--refresh --accept-drift`; ordinary checks are offline and must not update mtimes or provenance.
- `tests/e2e/coverage.json` is generated by `scripts/generate-e2e-coverage.mjs`. Update the `automated` map and run `pnpm coverage:generate`.

## E2E operation-level reconciliation

`scripts/e2e-reconcile.mjs` cross-references the coverage ledger against the vitest JSON report and the invoked-ops journal. Verdicts:

- **PASS**: at least one invocation where `expectError === isError` (both `true` for error-contract tests, both `false` for success-expected calls).
- **PARTIAL**: the scenario has a failing `it()` OR the op was invoked but no invocation matched its expected outcome.
- **NOT RUN**: the scenario is absent from the vitest report, or the suite passed but the op was never invoked.

Reconcile exits non-zero on any PARTIAL or NOT RUN. `pnpm e2e:jira` must not be committed against a non-zero reconcile.

### Run evidence chain

`scripts/e2e.mjs` writes `.e2e-state/<product>/run-manifest.json` at run start (`gitSha`, `dirty` plus truncated `dirtyFiles`, `startedAt`, `product`, `dockerImageDigest`, probed `productVersion`, `coverageSha` of `tests/e2e/coverage.json`, `policySha` of `src/exposure-policy.json`) and embeds the same fields into `.e2e-state/<product>/run-report.json`, making the report self-contained. Starting a run deletes that product's previous report and manifest; other products' state directories are left untouched.

Reconcile exits non-zero when the run report is missing, and when any embedded evidence field is stale: `gitSha` ≠ current HEAD, `dirty == true`, `coverageSha`/`policySha` mismatch the current generated artifacts, or `startedAt` predates the HEAD commit time. `--allow-stale` bypasses only these evidence checks (with a prominent warning) for development debugging; release flows must not use it. `scripts/e2e.mjs` likewise exits non-zero when the run's residual sweep failed, unless `--allow-sweep-failures` is passed (exploratory runs only).

### Release evidence chain

- Reconcile core logic lives in `scripts/lib/e2e-reconcile.mjs` (inputs: coverage ledger, vitest JSON report, invoked-ops journal; output: structured verdict object). Both the `scripts/e2e-reconcile.mjs` CLI and `scripts/release-check.mjs` consume it — never parse CLI stdout.
- `.e2e-state/<product>/` (gitignored) holds `run-manifest.json`, `run-report.json`, and `invoked-ops.jsonl` per product.
- `scripts/release-check.mjs` is the release-candidate gate. It requires a clean workspace; a report/manifest pair per product proving the exact HEAD (or the SHA passed via `--proven-sha <sha>`, used on the evidence commit and by the release workflow); manifest/report field agreement; and operation-level reconciliation against the `tests/e2e/coverage.json` automated ledger — expected counts are derived from the ledger per product, never hardcoded. Every operation must be PASS (zero PARTIAL / NOT RUN), `numTotalTests > 0`, zero failed tests. On success it writes `release-evidence/<gitSha>.json` (committed) with per-product operation counts and SHA-256 of report/manifest/journal; on any failure it exits non-zero and writes nothing.
- There are deliberately no `--allow-stale` / `--allow-sweep-failures` escape hatches in release-check; regression tests keep it that way.

### expectError flag

Pass `{ expectError: true }` as the third argument to `client.callTool()` for:

- Error-contract tests (e.g., an op that always returns 404 for new projects)
- Delete-then-verify calls (op expected to return `isError: true` after deletion)

Success-expected calls (the default, `expectError: false`) are verified by `requireToolSuccess`.

## CI contract

- `pnpm test:ci` runs: dependency pinning gate (`deps:check` — all deps exact-pinned, all runtime deps in `bundleDependencies`) → eslint → prettier format check → typecheck → build → unit tests with v8 coverage thresholds → contract tests → `coverage:check` → generated operations/inventory/policy checks → `env:check` → package smoke (staging pack via `scripts/pack.mjs`, then a fully `npm install --offline` of the packed tarball in an empty consumer directory — the bundle must be complete, and bundled versions must equal the pins).
- Coverage thresholds live in `vitest.config.ts` (`coverage.thresholds`) as the single source of truth (see "Unit coverage gate" in `docs/en/test-strategy.md`); raise them as coverage improves.
- `pnpm lint` (eslint) and `pnpm format:check` (prettier over the whole repo, excluding `.prettierignore` entries) are hard gates; both also run inside `pnpm test:ci`, and `git diff --check` runs in the CI lint job.
- CI matrix: Node 22 + 24 × Ubuntu + Windows. Windows runs the cross-platform subset (lint, typecheck, unit, contract, package smoke); unix-only cases are marked `it.skipIf(process.platform === "win32")`, and the coverage gate is Linux-only.
- Fixed generation/check commands: `node rule/fetch-api-inventory.mjs --refresh --bootstrap`, `pnpm inventory:check`, `pnpm operations:generate`, `pnpm operations:check`, `pnpm policy:generate`, `pnpm policy:check`.
- `pnpm coverage:check` validates the coverage ledger against the codebase. It greps each automated `operationId` in its scenario test file; named-tool-covered ops match via `NAMED_TOOL_SOURCES`.
- E2E tests are local-only (require licensed Atlassian Docker containers).

## Long-term documentation

- `README.md`, `README.zh-CN.md`, `docs/en/architecture.md`,
  `docs/en/exposure-policy.md`, `docs/en/test-strategy.md`,
  `docs/en/tool-contracts.md`, and
  `docs/en/release-process.md` are maintained entry points. English is the
  authoritative version; `docs/zh-CN/` holds the Chinese counterparts, and
  `docs/wiki/en|zh-CN/` holds the user-facing Wiki content source.
- `docs/en/test-strategy.md` is the single E2E developer document; the old
  `local-testing.md` was merged into it.
- `rule/api-inventory-official.md` is a machine-parsed data source (read by
  `scripts/generate-operations.mjs` and `rule/fetch-api-inventory.mjs`), not
  documentation; there is deliberately no zh-CN copy.
- `assets/banner.svg` is the hand-written README banner; keep it dependency
  free (system font stack only). README images and badges use absolute URLs
  so the npm package page renders them.
- Docs describe mechanisms and decisions, never point-in-time state: no
  hand-written operation counts, tier distributions, limit values, or
  measured coverage numbers. Numbers live in generated artifacts
  (`src/exposure-policy.json`, coverage ledger), in `vitest.config.ts`
  thresholds, or are runtime-queryable (`atlassian_discover_operations`,
  `doctor`). Upload/download limits are documented only in the wiki
  Attachments-and-Large-Results page.
- `pnpm env:check` (`scripts/check-env-docs.mjs`, part of `test:ci`) asserts
  every environment variable named in wiki Authentication-and-TLS /
  Client-Configuration is actually read by `src/config.ts`; undocumented
  code keys are warnings only.

## Commit conventions

- Commit in logical batches scoped to a fix-list item; the subject names the
  item (e.g. `R1: raise jira sprint update operations to risky tier`) and the
  body summarizes the why and any follow-ups.
- Note known residuals in commit messages: `jira.project.avatar.create` (deferred), scenario-level PARTIAL granularity. (run-report.json staleness was fixed by the run-evidence chain: reconcile now binds gitSha/dirty/coverage/policy SHA and exits non-zero on stale reports.)
